definitions.explanation: A Japanese green tea made by roasting tea leaves at high temperatures. It has a distinctive brown color, toasty aroma, and mild flavor with low caffeine content.

examples.japanese: ⟦{食後|しょくご}→食後：09499_shokugo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ほうじ{茶|ちゃ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飲|の}む→飲む：00322_nomu⟧。
ほうじ{茶|ちゃ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦カフェイン→カフェイン：27911_kafein⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{少|すく}ない→少ない：01136_sukunai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で⟦{夜|よる}→夜：00487_yoru⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{飲|の}める→飲む：00322_nomu⟧。
examples.english: Houjicha is low in caffeine, so you can drink it even at night.

examples.japanese: ⟦{最近|さいきん}→最近：00881_saikin⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧ほうじ{茶|ちゃ}ラテやほうじ{茶|ちゃ}⟦アイス→アイス：06770_aisu⟧⟦など→〜など：03095_nado⟧、ほうじ{茶|ちゃ}⟦{味|あじ}→味：00826_aji⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦スイーツ→スイーツ：27370_suiitsu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{人気|にんき}→人気：01488_ninki⟧だ。
examples.english: Recently, houjicha-flavored sweets like houjicha lattes and houjicha ice cream have become popular.

notes: Can also be written as {焙|ほう}じ{茶|ちゃ}, though the hiragana form is more common. One of the main types of Japanese tea alongside ⟦{煎茶|せんちゃ}→煎茶：13407_sencha⟧ (sencha), ⟦{玉露|ぎょくろ}→玉露：13595_gyokuro⟧ (gyokuro), ⟦{抹茶|まっちゃ}→抹茶：10574_maccha⟧ (matcha), and ⟦{番茶|ばんちゃ}→番茶：13724_bancha⟧ (bancha). Its low caffeine and gentle flavor make it popular with children and the elderly. In recent years, ほうじ{茶|ちゃ} has become a trendy flavor for lattes, ice cream, and other sweets.
